title: Tenant egress shield proxy for EU data sovereignty enforcement
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem statement: We need an enforcement point at the edge that guarantees EU-only data residency for tenants that require it, while still allowing predictable fallbacks when capacity or model variants are constrained. Current routing happens post-auth in the control plane which is too late for some compliance scenarios and does not produce a compact audit trail.

Goal: Implement a tenant-scoped egress shield proxy that evaluates residency policies before requests leave the customer boundary. The shield should: (1) enforce hard deny for non-EU egress when tenant policy requires EU-only; (2) implement allowlist/denylist overrides at tenant and org levels; (3) support soft-fallback to EU-hosted compatible model variants (no-external-egress variants) with clear telemetry; (4) provide an auditable, compact log record for every decision.

Design summary:
- Enforcement layer lives as an L7 sidecar (edge-proxy) in the dataplane between auth and routing. It evaluates a compact policy token (X-Residency-Policy) populated by the control plane or derived from tenant metadata.
- Policy decision is resolved via a new PDP (policy decision service) endpoint with very small JSON responses (action: allow|deny|fallback|passthrough) to minimize latency. PDP uses tenant allow/deny lists and region constraints.
- Precedence rules: explicit tenant denylist > tenant allowlist > org allowlist > org denylist > global default. Emergency passthrough requires a temporary authorization token and an audit entry.
- Fallback semantics: when PDP returns fallback, the proxy attempts to route to the tenant's pinned EU model variant or to the platform-compatible "no-egress" model variant. If neither is available, the request fails fast with a 451 and a structured explanation.
- Audit records: single-line JSON entries emitted to our audit topic (kafka-audit.shards) including fields: timestamp, tenant_id, decision, reason_code, model_variant, routed_region, request_id, actor. These logs feed Console's compliance dashboard.
- Observability: new metrics emitted by the proxy: residency_decisions_total{action}, residency_blocked_total, residency_fallback_rate, residency_latency_p50/p90. Traces include PDP latency and routing step.
- Config surfaces: tenant metadata in config-service (allowlist/denylist, residency_mode: EU_ONLY|PREFERRED|NONE), route table hints, and model_catalog flags for no-egress variants.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Latency vs correctness: local caching of PDP responses reduces RTT but increases staleness risk; we will use a short TTL (30s) with immediate invalidation on policy change.
- Complexity: introducing a sidecar increases deployment complexity for Dedicated and Private; kernel: we will ship this as an opt-in sidecar for Private in the first pass and enable by default in Hosted.
- Rollbacks: emergency passthrough is intentionally gated and requires two engineer approvals recorded in audit logs to prevent silent breaches.

Acceptance criteria:
- Edge proxy evaluates residency policies in <6ms p90 and produces audit entries for 100% of decisions.
- PDP cache TTL default 30s; policy change triggers immediate invalidation for affected tenant keys.
- Soft-fallback success rate >95% in canary tenants; fallback->failed responses return 451 with structured error for clients.
- Console shows residency_decisions_total and residency_blocked_total for tenants in the canary cohort.

Testing & rollout:
- Unit and integration tests for precedence logic, fallback selection, and audit entry generation.
- Load test using synthetic requests to validate p95 latency and cache behavior.
- Canary rollout: 5 tenants (internal) -> 25 external customers -> global. Feature flag: ff.geo_residency_shield.

Operational runbooks:
- Fast mitigation: toggle ff.geo_residency_shield or move tenant to PREFERRED mode in config-service.
- Audit check: daily job to validate that tenants with residency_mode=EU_ONLY have zero non-EU routed requests.

Notes about data model updates: config-service schema adds fields: residency_mode, allowlist_emails, denylist_accounts, emergency_passthrough_window_minutes. Model catalog adds attribute: egress_scope: EU_ONLY|GLOBAL|NO_EGRESS.
